parsed.main_gap: The graph argument falsely claims that fewer edges than vertices forbids cycles and loops; only the existence of at least one tree component follows.

errors.description: A multigraph with fewer edges than vertices may still contain a loop or cycle in one component, with other vertices isolated. Thus the component containing a_q need not be bipartite. The proof is repaired by choosing any tree component, whose existence follows from the total edge count.
errors.quote: Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on v vertices already uses at least v edges; hence every connected component C has e_C=v_C-1 and is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component containing the vertex of a_q.

parsed.notes: Apart from this localized, straightforwardly repairable graph-theoretic error, the drafting lemma, refinement construction, subset-sum bound, and binary lower-bound strategy form a coherent complete solution.
